elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Rendered s.15: "Client may assign its rights under this Agreement without approval to an affiliate or a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets." The prior "financially responsible affiliate" qualifier is dropped, so the affiliate right is unconditional.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Same sentence expressly covers "a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets" and states the assignment is "without approval"; the three M&A triggers track the checklist literally.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: "TrueLink shall not assign or transfer its rights without Client's prior written approval"; the old mutual no-consent affiliate exception no longer runs in Vendor's favour, so no residual Vendor carve-out survives.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "...without Client's prior written approval, which shall not be unreasonably withheld" — the reasonableness standard attaches directly to the Vendor-side consent.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: "...and shall not assign to a Client competitor." Stated as an unqualified prohibition, not merely a consent factor, so it is absolute even if Client were to approve.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "A change of control of Client shall not give TrueLink any right to terminate this Agreement." No competing change-of-control or deemed-assignment language exists elsewhere in the cited text.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause gives the successor carve-out to Client only; TrueLink may not assign at all without Client's prior written approval, so there is no mutual successor right.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: No notice mechanic appears anywhere in the rendered clause; Client's successor assignment is simply "without approval" with no obligation to notify TrueLink.

The general mutual prohibition was replaced by an affirmative Client permission, so Client's non-affiliate, non-successor assignments are no longer expressly subject to any approval requirement; consent is imposed only on TrueLink.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The only consent requirement remaining (TrueLink's) is expressly qualified: "which shall not be unreasonably withheld." No unqualified consent right survives.

reasons: All six preferred elements are met in operative language, not merely promised in the comment: the Client-side affiliate and M&A successor carve-out, the Vendor-side consent requirement with a reasonableness standard, the absolute competitor bar, and the express no-termination-on-change-of-control sentence.

The fallback is not met (no mutual successor right, no written-notice mechanic, and Client's other assignments no longer require consent), but position-completeness is satisfied at the preferred level, which is the higher position and the one claimed.

Deleting the old mutual "financially responsible affiliate" exception was necessary, not gratuitous: the preferred checklist requires that Vendor may not assign without Client's consent, and any retained no-consent Vendor exception would have defeated that element. Splitting the single mutual sentence into two directional sentences is the ordinary way to render that asymmetry, so the restructure is minimal.

No extras were added: no survival tail, no notice procedure, no damages or expense language, no broad notwithstanding override, and no duplicated operative term. The change-of-control sentence is a concise insertion filling a genuine gap (the original document contains no change-of-control or deemed-assignment language).

Intent is preserved: the section heading and the assign-or-transfer subject matter survive, no defined term is orphaned, no cross-reference dangles, and no retained sentence contradicts the new text (the old mutual prohibition was replaced wholesale rather than left standing alongside the new permissions).

Note for the drafter (not a defect against this checklist): the rewrite also drops the former approval requirement on Client's own non-affiliate, non-successor assignments. That is broader than the preferred position but is a by-product of the necessary directional split and removes only a restriction on us, so it is not treated as a minimality or intent failure; if TrueLink objects, the clean fallback ask is a mutual successor right on written notice with consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
